about: Exercises with PhET simulations (CC-BY), placed into rooms. Answers checked against the simulations: notes/phet/build_phet.py.

enc.title: PhET: Wien and Stefan–Boltzmann on real stars

sim.name: PhET Blackbody Spectrum
sim.setup: Tick Graph Values, Labels and Intensity. Drag the thermometer or click its labels: Earth 250 K, Light Bulb 3000 K, Sun 5800 K, Sirius A 9950 K. Zoom the axes with the magnifiers.
sim.credit: PhET Interactive Simulations, University of Colorado Boulder (CC-BY).

enc.problem: The curve is the spectral exitance $\pi B_\lambda(T)$ in MW m$^{-2}\,\mu$m$^{-1}$; Wien: $\lambda_{\max}T=2.898\times10^{-3}$ m K; total intensity $\sigma T^4$.

steps.prompt: Sirius A (9950 K): wavelength of the peak ($\mu$m).
steps.hint: $2898\ \mu$m K / 9950 K = 0.291 $\mu$m: ultraviolet. Sirius looks blue-white.

steps.prompt: Intensity of Sirius A relative to the Sun (ratio of the two readouts).
Ratio of the peak heights Sirius A / Sun.
steps.hint: The peak value scales as $T^5$ ($B_\lambda\propto\lambda^{-5}$ at $\lambda_{\max}\propto1/T$): $14.9$; the sim shows 84.45 and 1255 MW m$^{-2}\mu$m$^{-1}$.

steps.prompt: From the Sun's intensity readout, the solar luminosity $L=4\pi R_\odot^2\sigma T^4$ ($R_\odot=6.96\times10^8$ m), in W.
Earth (250 K): peak wavelength ($\mu$m). Zoom out to find it.
steps.hint: 11.6 $\mu$m: thermal infrared, where greenhouse gases absorb. Bolometric intensity only 222 W m$^{-2}$.

source.where: Blackbody Spectrum 1.0: presets 250/3000/5800/9950 K; readouts at 5800 K: peak 84.45 MW/m^2/um at 0.500 um, 6.42e7 W/m^2 (checked in the sim)
